memories.content: HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess the reproducibility of results if the prototype version used in the evaluation is not disclosed.
Record the manipulated and fixed elements of compared design alternatives so that other researchers can reconstruct them.
Records of formative evaluation decisions enable the reconstruction of connections between raw data, interpretation, and design modifications.
The user must make it possible to trace which observations each prototype version reflects so the process of deriving design knowledge can be reviewed.
Calculate user research compensation budgets based on the estimated participation burden, combining session time with required technical and travel preparation.
Compensate participants who withdraw from the study midway for their actual participation time.
Compensate for the time actually spent in sessions, regardless of the research modality.
Allow the issuance of gift cards of equivalent value to participants in remote studies who cannot use electronic transfers.
Do not treat an unresolved payment method as a deficiency at the proposal stage.
Allow differential compensation amounts for on-site and remote studies when participation burden varies due to travel or technical preparation.
Participants judge the fairness of compensation based on the combined burden of session time and required technical and travel preparation.
In longitudinal studies requiring diary entries and repeated reporting, include out-of-session recording time in compensation calculations.
Distinguish between participant research compensation and labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as part of their duties.
The user tends to count session time but omit participants’ advance setup and follow-up reporting time.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains. The reference frame focuses on documenting prototype provenance and design-evaluation decisions for reproducibility, while the compared frame establishes participant-compensation principles covering burden, timing, payment methods, study conditions, and role boundaries.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only requirement about identifying the evaluated artifact; the compared frame contains no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Evaluations should disclose the prototype version used so reviewers can assess reproducibility.

relations.reason: This reference-only claim concerns documenting experimental design differences and is independent of the compensation policies in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Researchers should record manipulated and fixed elements of design alternatives to support reconstruction.

relations.reason: The reference memories split one provenance requirement: preserving reviewable connections between evaluation evidence, decisions, modifications, and successive prototypes. No compared memory addresses this requirement.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation records should trace observations and raw data through interpretation to design modifications and prototype versions.

relations.reason: These compared memories provide the rationale, budgeting rule, modality consequence, and recurring omission for one burden-based compensation policy. The reference frame has no corresponding compensation claim.
relations.summary: Compensation should reflect total participation burden, including session time and required technical or travel preparation, allowing modality-based differences when burden differs.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only rule for the specific case of mid-study withdrawal and is independently useful from general burden calculation.
relations.summary: Participants who withdraw midway should be compensated for their actual participation time.

relations.reason: This compared-only baseline applies across remote and on-site sessions and is distinct from adjustments for preparation, travel, withdrawal, or longitudinal reporting.
relations.summary: Time actually spent in research sessions should be compensated regardless of modality.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only policy about an alternative payment instrument under a stated accessibility condition.
relations.summary: Remote participants unable to use electronic transfers may receive gift cards of equivalent value.

relations.reason: This compared-only evaluation rule concerns when payment logistics must be settled, rather than compensation amount or burden.
relations.summary: An unresolved payment method should not be treated as a proposal-stage deficiency.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only rule scoped to longitudinal out-of-session recording work.
relations.summary: Compensation for longitudinal studies should include time spent on diary entries and repeated reporting outside sessions.

relations.reason: This compared-only accounting boundary separates participant burden payments from employee or contractor labor costs.
relations.summary: Participant research compensation should be distinguished from labor costs for field staff performing installation and operational support as job duties.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame uniquely bases compensation on actual and total participation burden, with provisions for withdrawal, modality, longitudinal reporting, payment alternatives, proposal-stage uncertainty, and separation of participant payments from staff labor costs.
reports.reference_only: The reference uniquely requires disclosure of evaluated prototype versions, reconstruction of design alternatives, and traceability from observations and raw data through interpretation to prototype changes.
